speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The next morning, on Tuesday, 6 March, Speaker informed me that the Leader of the House also wished to make a statement on the matter.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I was not informed of when the Leader would do so.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Leader subsequently made a statement that same morning at the start of the Sitting while I was on my way to Parliament.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: She has extended a copy of her statement to me by email.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Speaker, Sir, after the debate on 1 March, I had time to track back what led me to have the impression and suspicions I articulated during the exchanges with the Ministers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Since 2013, the Prime Minister had said that our expected increases in spending would require more tax revenue.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat had also made a similar statement in last year's Budget, saying that the Government was studying how it would raise revenue through new taxes or raising tax rates.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These statements were very general and did not specify any timeframe for the raising of taxes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Prime Minister's statement was made on 19 November 2017 with the Budget Statement for 2018 just three months away.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Literally, these announcements concerning tax increases set off public discussion and speculation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Three days later, on 22 November 2017, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) issued a statement that Prime Minister Lee's announcement at the PAP Convention was in line with a much earlier statement made by Deputy Prime Minister Tharman when he was Finance Minister in 2015.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Tharman had then said that the revenue measures that the Government had already undertaken would provide sufficiently for increased spending planned until the end of the decade.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In reporting the MOF statement, Channel NewsAsia (CNA) commented as follows, and I quote, "The Ministry's statement came after Mr Lee's comments on the impending tax hike triggered public discussion that the Government is making a U-turn." MOF further stated that planning for the issue now would allow the Ministry to, and I quote, "better ease in the needed measures and to give our people and businesses some time to adjust".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The MOF statement did not definitively say that there would be no tax increase in this Budget.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The fact is, raising taxes in the Budget and only announcing it in the Budget Statement was what the Government had done in the past.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Hence, the uncertainty over whether taxes and, in particular, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) would be raised in this Budget continued even after the MOF statement.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This was further fuelled when MOF officeholders kept up the discussion on raising taxes in the immediate run-up to the Budget Statement, saying they were working on when.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Prominent economists went on record to predict that the GST rate would be raised in 2018 or 2019.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Such economists included those from the United Overseas Bank (UOB), Ernst & Young and the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As an Opposition Member of Parliament (MP), it is my duty to watch every move and signal from the Government for the future of Singapore and the welfare of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Hence, I admit that I did suspect that the Government intended to raise the GST.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: However, the Government contributed to this suspicion by its non-denial of reports and economists' predictions of an immediate GST rise.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Based on the sequence of events, I believed that the Government could have intended to raise the GST at this Budget.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Thus, during the heat of the exchanges at the Budget Round-up, I articulated my suspicion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In doing so, I believe I was doing my duty as an MP to convey ground concerns, reactions and confusion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I did not accuse the Government of being untruthful as alleged, and neither had I intended to accuse the Government of dishonesty.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I do not accept the over-characterisation the PAP MPs have put on my words and intentions, based on their own interpretation borne out of over-active imaginations and over-sensitivity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Since the Government has now refuted that it had any intention to raise GST immediately, I can accept that my suspicion then may not have been correct.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Leader, do you have any response to the clarification?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She made the accusation, she made the statement in the House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At that time, she did not have the facts with her.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Minister for Finance put the facts squarely before the House, inviting her to question as a witness.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: She did not make any attempt to do that.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So, here you are, Minister for Finance, together with the Prime Minister with Deputy Prime Minister, putting their statements, explaining to the House their plans all along, they had been thinking about it, in the long run, planning for tax increases for the next decade.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And you have an MP coming here to make statements that basically accuse them of doing otherwise.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Lim is saying that the Government is saying one thing in public but planning secretly to do another.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So, I am disappointed that she has failed to apologise to the House for making these false allegations.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The allegations have, indeed, harmed and tarnished the reputations of other Members, namely, the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Heng Swee Keat, because she has put questions, she has not withdrawn the allegations, she has not apologised.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I think the privilege that Parliamentarians enjoy come with responsibility, that whatever we say here, if you do not have the facts, you should check them, and having checked so, you should consider whether the remarks have, indeed, hurt the integrity of the Members.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And I put to the House that, indeed, they have.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So, I would just like to remind Members of the House that they may not abuse this privilege to misrepresent facts or mislead Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are not entitled to make unsubstantiated allegations without taking steps to check the facts or knowingly maintain the allegations they have been shown to have no factual basis.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Unlike her colleague Non-Constituency MP Leon Perera, who both withdrew and apologised to this House for making misleading statements in a recent case, Ms Lim has refused to apologise.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I would just like to make two points at this stage, depending on where the Speaker wants to take this debate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If the Government had, indeed, been so clear of its intentions not to raise GST before 2021, why is it that the public was so worried that this would happen?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Why was it that the economists came up with reports after the Prime Minister's speech at the PAP Convention to predict that the GST rate would be increased in this Budget?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And I would like to quote this statement from Cabinet which was made in the House quite recently.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I begin the quote, "If MPs believe that something is wrong, it is MP's job to pursue the facts and make these allegations in their name, decide whether something seems to be wrong and if you think something is wrong, even if you are not fully sure, then come to this House, confront the Government, ask for explanations and answers." This is a quote from Prime Minister Lee during the closing debate on 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like the Leader to clarify.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: One standard when the Prime Minister's name needs to be cleared and another standard when we are talking about raising taxes on the people?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this Chamber, we often make representations and bring forth the views from our constituents, from our stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are MPs; most of us are elected to do so, to be the voice of the people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are fully expected to do so, there is nothing wrong with it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we have a responsibility when we bring this matter to this place.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because this Chamber is for serious debate, is for making laws, is where we have serious discussions about the future of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, before we bring the opinions, the speculations, the views, the unhappiness, to this Chamber, we need to check the facts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Lim has admitted that she did not do so in the first instance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But having said so, after she has brought the matter here, we have laid down the facts to her.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Finance Minister had plainly said that there was not such an intention.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And yet, she continued to insist on that allegation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is the matter that we are discussing here.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And this is the difference between what we say in this Chamber and what economists, analysts say outside this Chamber.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have a duty to fellow Members, we have a duty to fellow Singaporeans that whatever we say here carries responsibility.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe she has been quite clear on that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I thought I made it very clear that I am not retracting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I thought that Ms Lim has admitted that those were her suspicion and that she would retract it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But that being the case, I must say that we are deeply disappointed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For someone of her experience should accuse the Government for lack of candour, even though the facts had been explained to her clearly, both in the public domain in statements made by MOF as well as here, by the Minister for Finance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I repeat again – it is expected of us to bring our views forth here.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But if the facts were wrong, and we have said that the facts were wrong, we had not had this plan of floating a balloon, only to retract after public pressure, that is just not existent, it is a figment of her imagination, she continues with this accusation, which is deeply disappointing and deplorable.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I have permitted both sides of the House to state their respective positions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister for Finance, would you like to add?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I think Ms Lim made a statement on 1 March and let me quote, "We do know that in the run-up to the Budget discussion, there were some test balloons being floated out about the fact that the Government needs to raise revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And immediately the public seized on the fact that Deputy Prime Minister Tharman and perhaps other leaders had earlier said that the Government has enough money for the decade.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, the public pointed out, 'Hey, you know, is this a contradiction?' And I rather suspect", "I" meaning Ms Sylvia Lim, "that the Government is stuck with that announcement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Lim was, in fact, accusing the Government of being untruthful when it says that it had planned ahead and that its proposal to raise the GST between 2021 and 2025 was a result of such planning.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Lim asked earlier why is it that MOF did not come out to reveal details at the Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We take great care in preparing the Budget and that the details are kept as secret until the day of the Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Because it has got impact on the market, not just in Singapore but internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I do think that these are serious matters.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What Ms Lim is saying is that your allegations, you made the allegations, you claim to reflect the views of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But you said "I suspect that this is the case".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unless you have a basis for that, that you cannot come here and say, "I heard this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, having examined all the facts, do you have a basis?

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And if not, I think it is only right and proper that you withdraw the statement.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I do not think the Minister for Finance was listening to my speech.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I set out in my speech the basis for my suspicions, going through the chronology of events that led me, and not only me, others to have that suspicion.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Minister for Finance mentioned that, of course, Budget preparation is a secret and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And I think that is part of the whole issue.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I do not accept that my suspicion had no basis.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I do take it that Budget is a serious matter, and there is always secrecy because it might affect market movements and all that.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: But since the Government has no intention to raise GST, I think there is nothing wrong for the Government to come up earlier to say that, "Look, we do not have the intention to raise GST at this Budget." That would have cleared the air and the confusion on the ground of speculation that, "Well, you are keeping quiet, you are raising tax, but not mentioning what kind of tax." GST is a form of tax.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And that, I think, contributed to ground confusion, and leading to the impression formed.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I can understand that in the heat of exchange, that it comes to your mind, you articulated that.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I think Ms Lim accepted that that was at the point in time and now it is clear that the Government has no intention to raise GST.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: And her suspicion was not really correct – at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I duly note the positions stated by both sides of the House unless there are any other points to be raised by either side that would provide further clarity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I think I can accept that in the heat of the exchange, you may be saying things which you did not intend.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In fact, the issue of raising taxes had been raised many times before that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is just that the timing and the details are not revealed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As I have said earlier, I duly note the positions stated by both sides of the House.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the day.
